Every count matches the plan row 4.15 and green-4.15.txt: review-run 96 pass, judge-run 48, quota 31, adversarial-p4-runner 15, adversarial-p4c 13, decode-parity 4, adjudicate 23, review-score 27, adversarial-p4b 12. Each 4.15 fix matches its section 14.5 contract: N21, N9, N10, N11, N26, N27, N28, N30, N31, N32, E1, and N13. The AA1, AA2, JA1, and JA2 text change is the N31 contract. It removes no assertion. nonblocking_findings: F1 [High, nonblocking under the PM round cap] The new exe-path filter in daemon_pids skips the live daemon shape. review-run.sh:502-503 and judge-run.sh:376-377 drop a pid when argv[0] holds a path outside the job root. The live incident shape is `/home/daniebo/.nvm/versions/node/v24.19.0/lib/node_modules/@opencode/cli/bin/opencode.exe serve --service` (measure/runs/opencode_host_isolation/record-3.1.log). That exe exists outside every job root. I ran the extracted production block over a synthetic proc table with that argv[0] and HOME and cwd inside the job root. It selected no pid. The P4B-C1 local control uses a bare `node` argv[0] (adversarial-p4-runner.test.ts:938), so it cannot fail on the real shape. The exit-time opencode_host_cleanup still stops marked processes by BENCH_OPENCODE_JOB (opencode-host.sh:35-48). The per-pass guard and its INFRA record no longer match. Fix: key the scope on the BENCH_OPENCODE_JOB marker, and add a case with a path-form exe outside the job root.

F2 [Medium, nonblocking] The judge shell decoder is not behavior-identical to the two TS decoders. judge-run.sh:1120 still pushes a `result` event text into `parts`, while review-score.ts:261 and adjudicate.ts:250 push it into `resultParts` and drop it when text parts exist. I ran both algorithms in node on a stream with a top-level `result` event and `text` events. The shell answer kept the forged result block and the TS answer dropped it. The comments at judge-run.sh:1099, review-score.ts:229, and adjudicate.ts:218 still say `the same decoder`. The N13 judge fixture (decode-parity.test.ts:600-610) feeds the shell a different shape, so it pins the filter only for a nested JSON line. No key leaks and the pinned parity passes, so it is nonblocking.

F3 [Low] The N32 group sits only in quota.test.ts:889. The strategy row 14.5 names review-run.test.ts and judge-run.test.ts too. review-run.test.ts:1895 only checks that the reason holds the word `quota`. No runner case pins the raw loopback reason out of stdout or a record. The quota.ts fix removes the raw string at the source (quota.ts:277), so the code is safe. The named runner coverage is absent.

F4 [Low] The N26 case (review-run.test.ts:4381-4405) asserts only `stdout.length <= 500`. An empty error line would pass. The case does not run a probe or write a record, while the strategy says a 300 KB line gives a record and exit 0. The production cut at review-run.sh:944 and judge-run.sh:714 is correct.

F5 [Low] The N10 symlink walk and the N27 token rule also landed in judge-run.sh (lines 556 and 153), but only review-run.test.ts pins them. The strategy rows N10 and N27 name review-run.test.ts only. A later drift in the judge copy has no test. Separately, the N10 walk refuses any symlink at or below a call path (review-run.sh:792, judge-run.sh:556), not only a link that resolves outside the root. The refusal message says `out of the job root`. It is fail-closed, but broader than the stated contract.

F6 [Low] plan.md:2503-2505 still says error_line_of prints `the error output held a credential value` when scan_output exits 2. Task 4.15 N31 changes that path to `the error output could not be scanned`. The 4.13ab entry is historical, but a reader can take it as current.

N21, N9, N10, N11, N26, N27, N28 fixes match the 14.5 contracts. N21 adds the three UTF-8 byte patterns E2 80 AE, C2 85, and E2 80 8B to read_message_line (review-run.sh:373-376); the case fails when the byte check is absent. N9 suppresses the INFRA line when the start time changed (review-run.sh:563-570, judge-run.sh:439-446); the case has a positive control and a reused-pid control. N10 walks each call path with `find -mindepth 0 -type l` (review-run.sh:790-796, judge-run.sh:554-560). N11 requires adjacent `serve` then `--service` (review-run.sh:496-500, judge-run.sh:370-374). N26 cuts the line to 499 content bytes before the scan (review-run.sh:944, judge-run.sh:714). N27 clears `tokens_complete` when a field sum is not a safe integer (review-run.sh:195, judge-run.sh:153). N28 clears `error_line` on a reachable probe (review-run.sh:1076).

N30, N31, F1, and E1 fixes match the 14.5 contracts. `ERROR_SCAN_TEXT` is exactly `the error output could not be scanned` (review-run.sh:859, judge-run.sh:623) and prints only on scan exit 2. The found-key text stays for a real found key. AA1, AA2, JA1, and JA2 now expect the scan-fail text; every other assertion, including the no-key checks, stays. The N30 probe and judge start-test cases assert the fixed text and no key; the fixture puts the key in the stdout error event. E1 is un-skipped (`it`, adversarial-p4c.test.ts:907) and passes; `error_all_events_text` joins the first line of every error event and greps the values file (review-run.sh:967-971, judge-run.sh:728-733).

N32: quota.ts:275-277 returns `the quota source reported an error` and drops the loopback string. The case at quota.test.ts:889 asserts the raw marker `mg-n32-raw-quota-reason-0123456789` is absent from the first stderr line and the fixed text is present. F3 records the missing runner cases.

N13: review-score.ts and adjudicate.ts split `result` parts and drop them when text parts exist. judge-run.sh does not. My node run of the two algorithms on a stream with a top-level `result` event plus `text` events printed the shell answer with the forged block and the TS answer without it. The third N13 fixture for the judge is built from a text event that holds a JSON `result` line, so the shell filter is exercised for a nested line only. The decode-parity file passes 4 of 4 at HEAD.

The two error_line_of copies are byte-identical. The two daemon_pids copies are byte-identical. stop_daemons differs only in the runner name, and error_line_of differs only in the comment after the function. error_all_events_text and scan_output are byte-identical. Route parity holds for the two runners.

No real-key leak: `git diff 7d7d218..ff64dab | grep -E 'sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}|AKIA|ghp_|xox[bap]'` printed no line. The committed test keys are explicit fakes: `sk-test-credential-value-0123456789` and `sk-adv-runner-secret-...`. The production redaction prints fixed text. No page under docs/ changed.
